criteria.criterion: F-M2-2 is confirmed fixed: per-frame fov and silhouette traces of Exit at scroll 0 and a scrolled offset arrive with no step larger than the median of the preceding 10 frames, judged also by eye from the screencast.
criteria.evidence: fovtrace: scroll 0 last values 32.034, 32.01, 32.002, 32, 32, 32 with arrival step 0 (preceding-10 median 0.047); scroll 300 arrival step 0 (median 0.073); no step across the swap row. Silhouette at scroll 0 (bbox of the avatar in 72 screencast frames): 0 steps above the preceding-10 median, last steps 1 px or 0. At scroll 300 the on-screen motion after the swap is the page scroll restore: its wrap offset follows an ease-in-out and arrives with steps 2.7 then 0 px. The screencast dropped frames in the middle of that scroll leg, so its bbox is not trusted there and the per-frame DOM rows were used instead. Honest note: a strict all-frames application of the rule flags near-peak plateau samples (fov steps 1.449 vs median 1.221 at 380 ms and 1.554 vs 1.017 at 365 ms; wrap step 34.61 vs peak 34.66), which are the velocity peak of an ease-in-out, not the arrival; every step after the peak region toward arrival is below its preceding median. By eye in montage-exit-s0.jpg and montage-exit-s300.jpg: smooth settle, no jump, no pop at the swap.

decisionsProposed: Accept the useGLTF(url, true, false) edit in Avatar.tsx as recorded: verified neutral because no project GLB uses meshopt and the draco flag is unchanged.
lessonsProposed: Never pkill next-server by name to clean up a prod copy; kill the exact listener pid for the port you started, because the dev server and other agents' servers share that process name.
Judge an 'arrival with no larger step than the preceding median' rule on the arrival leg only; near the velocity peak of an ease-in-out, strict all-frames application flags the peak itself.
Bright-pixel silhouette bbox is invalid once page text scrolls into the region and Chrome screencast drops frames during scroll; use the per-frame DOM rect rows for scrolled exits.
